aipref-shared-training-opt-out-token-202.detail:
Its basis is an Internet-Draft titled Machine-Readable Training Preference Signal, written by Kevin Kelley of Anthropic and published October 30 under IETF's AI Preferences working group. It expires May 3, 2027. IETF's datatracker labels it an individual draft, not endorsed by IETF and without formal standing. It adds no new directive names or grammar: one example group reads User-Agent: __usage_ai-training, Disallow: /, Allow: /press-kit/. This token expresses preference about training, not whether pages may be fetched.

Google's John Mueller wrote that where sites opt out through this token without naming Google-Extended, Google plans to treat it as if Google-Extended had been disallowed, with support arriving in 2027 alongside other providers; Google called its proposal consistent with EU's code of practice for general-purpose AI model providers. Microsoft's Krishna Madhavan said Bing will honor this shared training preference from February 1, 2027, add its own page-level AI Grounding preference with DisallowExtended as one option, and stop reading NoArchive and NoCache tags as training or grounding preferences after March 1, 2027. OpenAI called this effort voluntary and said its existing crawler controls continue to apply.

Paul Thurrott of Thurrott.com called it largely symbolic, coming years after those companies took content at a scale he said had never been seen before. Nate Hake, who took part in that working group, wrote that work is not finished at IETF level and that significant areas of dispute remain.
